text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Canary traffic alert: 3.4x increase in queue length and 15-30% p50/p95 throughput drop on canary slice a3. Flags: canary=true, batch_prefetch=on. Triggered at 14:00 UTC.
Elena (oncall): seeing same in datadog. p95 up ~220ms -> 650ms on slice a3, other slices stable. Noted kernel-fallback spikes in logs.
Tom SRE: @Elena can you post last 60s of exporter logs? is it eviction or prefetch backlog?
Elena (oncall): attaching snippet: ```
[14:00:08] slice=a3 queue_len=128 pending_batches=42 kernel_fallback=true kv_hits=0.3
[14:00:12] slice=a3 qlen=192 pending_batches=60 kernel_fallback=true batch_delay_ms=120
```
Jun (runtime): kernel_fallback=true is suspect. Recent deploy changed batching router heuristics (canary only) to increase batch depth. Might be causing oversized batches and prefetch fanout.
Ana (support): any immediate customer impact? Support dashboard shows a handful of 5xx/L7-errors for enterprise org id=rdw-113 during the window, customers seeing timeouts at ~10s.
Jay (product): flagged customers = two paid tenants in EU. Need comms if rollback required.
Elena (oncall): I'm going to throttle canary to 20% traffic and flip canary feature flag to off if no improvement in 60s. Rolling throttle now via routemgr: `curl -XPOST /routes/canary -d '{"weight":20}'`
DeployBot: route update acknowledged, canary weight -> 20% (applied to region eu-west-1).
Tom SRE: after throttle, queue_len dropped to ~70, p95 to ~350ms but kernel_fallback still appearing intermittently. Root cause likely interplay between batch depth and KV prefetch concurrency.
Jun (runtime): can we disable batch_prefetch on canary (it's a feature flag) to validate? That was toggled in the same change. Command: `reroutectl flag set batch_prefetch=false --slice a3`
Elena (oncall): doing it now.
Elena (oncall): flag off applied. Observed: immediate drop in pending_batches to single digits, queue_len -> 24, p95 -> 210ms. Kernel-fallback logs stop.
Tom SRE: solid repro -> batching prefetch concurrency caused thrash and kernel fallback on this slice under canary routing. For mitigation: keep canary weight low, roll back feature flag globally from the release or patch batching heuristics.
Jay (product): propose full rollback of the canary change set (the batching heuristic commit) across all regions. Are there any safety concerns?
Jun (runtime): rollback safe. We also need a follow-up: tune batch depth limits and add a circuit-breaker to disable prefetch when queue_len > 100. I'll open an RFC.
Ana (support): ETA for rollback? customers impacted want a timeline.
Elena (oncall): we'll perform a controlled rollback in 10m then monitor 30m. I'll coordinate handoff to next shift.
DeployBot: rollback queued: release v2026.03.15-batch-heuristic -> reverting commit 7a2f3c. Estimated finish 14:12 UTC.
Tom SRE: running pre-rollback checks: verifying no other dependent flags. All clear.
Jun (runtime): pre-rollback validation ok. Post-rollback action items: revert batching heuristics, add unit + integration tests for prefetch concurrency, add metric for prefetch_concurrency to alert earlier.
Elena (oncall): rollback complete at 14:12 UTC. Immediate metrics: queue_len stable < 30 across all slices, p95 back to baseline ~180ms.
Ana (support): confirming enterprise tenant rdw-113 still reports a couple timeouts but clearing. Sending note to customers: "We detected higher latency for certain requests during a canary deploy and reverted the change. No further action required; we're monitoring."
Jay (product): thanks. We'll follow up with a postmortem and customer-facing blurb.
Tom SRE: adding interim mitigation: 1) keep canary weight capped at 10% for next 48h, 2) add temporary alert when kernel_fallback=true on any slice > 5 occurrences/min, 3) block merging of batching heuristic until tests + auto-circuit are in.
Jun (runtime): noted. I'll draft the postmortem + RCA. Root cause summary: aggressive batch_prefetch concurrency + increased batch depth under canary routing caused KV prefetch saturation -> kernel fallback -> queue growth.
Elena (oncall): Handoff to next oncall @Tom SRE in 30m. Please acknowledge.
Tom SRE: ack. I'll take watch and run the 30m post-rollback monitoring.
IncidentBot: Incident resolved: canary rollback applied, customer impact limited to transient timeouts for two enterprise tenants. Incident channel closed for active mitigation.
Elena (oncall): adding notes to pagerduty ticket PD-9921 and will create postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
